second_speaker_utterance_with_correspond: Private companies handling routine care do not fragment the NHS if properly regulated.
They can complement the system by efficiently managing routine services, freeing up NHS resources for complex cases.
Mixed systems like those in Denmark show that universal access and equity can coexist with private sector participation.
Full government control risks inefficiency and stagnation because monopolies lack the competitive pressure to innovate or improve service delivery.
The NHS's funding challenges are primarily due to mismanagement and lack of reform, not private sector cherry-picking.
